_comment: SPARK - S177 P4 (owner): THE TWO CINEMATICS THE VOLTKIN TV NEVER HAD.
Owner, S177, giving the general pipeline: "every structure has kind of the same few stances as a
creature would. It's just a kind of different pipeline. The first one is when you deploy structure,
him being built. Second one, when the structure is built, is when he stands idle - that's not
really a video, that's just a state, like a picture. But there's the video between one and two,
being built to idle. Then three, there's another state which is damaged. And then four is
destroyed, is another video. It's another state transition."
So a STRUCTURE needs exactly TWO clips and the rest are stills:
This is also exactly what the recipe file's subjectKind.BUILDING allows: 'Generate a clip only for
a genuine cinematic (the spawn burst, the crumble)', with staticSubject:true. The four remaining

S177 RE-ROLL #1: the first pair FAILED check-clip - 'SUBJECT TOUCHES THE FRAME EDGE, NOT RECOVERABLE' (spawning 4/24 frames, destroyed 7/24). Cause: the burst threw glass and debris to the frame edges, which also poisons the packer's union bbox and would have packed the TV tiny inside a debris-sized box. Fix: seed dropped 52% -> 40% height for margin, the action explicitly contained near centre, and a hard no-edge clause on every state. Rejected clips kept at clips/tv-rejected-s177/ rather than deleted.

spawning.prompt: a small battered vintage cathode-ray television set with a boxy wooden cabinet, stubby legs and a starburst-cracked glass screen, standing upright on the ground, shown SMALL in the centre of the frame with generous empty space all around it . The cracked screen bursts open and a small glowing lightning creature pushes its head and shoulders out through the broken screen and climbs clear of the cabinet , a single continuous burst-and-emerge . Only a few small glass shards fall, close to the set . Thin arcs of blue-white electricity crawl over its casing and the cracked screen flickers; it is old, heavy and charged with something it cannot hold. The television cabinet stays in the SAME SPOT the whole time , upright and square on , and does not tip , slide or travel . By the end of the clip the creature is out and clear and the set is left standing still with a blown-out empty screen . The ENTIRE television and every piece of glass, debris and smoke must stay FULLY INSIDE the frame with a wide clear margin on all four sides at all times ; nothing leaves the frame and nothing touches any edge of the frame . Keep the whole action small and tightly contained near the centre of the frame .
spawning._why: The deploy->idle transition. Seeded on tv-1-intact so the clip STARTS at the state the board already shows and ENDS at the blown-out screen the resting texture wears.

destroyed.prompt: a small battered vintage cathode-ray television set with a boxy wooden cabinet, stubby legs and a starburst-cracked glass screen, standing upright on the ground, shown SMALL in the centre of the frame with generous empty space all around it . The set is destroyed : it sparks , the cabinet breaks apart with a small puff of smoke , and the wreckage collapses straight DOWN ONTO THE GROUND into a motionless heap of broken panels directly beneath where it stood . The debris falls close and stays in a tight pile . Thin arcs of blue-white electricity crawl over its casing and the cracked screen flickers; it is old, heavy and charged with something it cannot hold. It stays in the SAME SPOT and does not travel . It is already coming apart by the middle of the clip , and for the entire second half the wreck lies completely still on the ground , not moving at all . The ENTIRE television and every piece of glass, debris and smoke must stay FULLY INSIDE the frame with a wide clear margin on all four sides at all times ; nothing leaves the frame and nothing touches any edge of the frame . Keep the whole action small and tightly contained near the centre of the frame .
destroyed._why: The crumble. Shaped on the proven `die` template (down by the halfway point, motionless second half) because that is the one prompt shape measured to end still and in frame.
